questions: Did the movements begin suddenly or reach their current severity within a few days?
Do the movements completely stop when you are asleep?
Can you voluntarily stop the movements, even briefly?
Do the movements change markedly in speed, size, or pattern from one moment to the next?
Do they lessen when you concentrate on the affected leg or worsen when you focus on them?
Do you feel an urge or uncomfortable sensation in the leg before each movement that is relieved by moving it?
Are the movements rhythmic and regular?
Do they occur mainly when the leg is at rest, especially in the evening or at night?
Are there sudden jerks, sustained abnormal postures, or twisting of the leg?
Have you had weakness, numbness, loss of balance, or difficulty walking in that leg?
Have you experienced loss of awareness, confusion, tongue biting, or loss of bladder control during the episodes?
Do the movements occur during voluntary actions such as walking or standing?
Did they begin after an injury, illness, operation, or other stressful event?
Have you started, stopped, or changed any medications or recreational substances before the movements began?
Have you had similar movements elsewhere in your body?
Does anyone in your family have a similar movement disorder?
Do you have a history of seizures, stroke, multiple sclerosis, Parkinson’s disease, or other neurological illness?
Do anxiety, emotional stress, or being observed make the movements worse?
